title: Fluorescent staining of cells on 3D broccoli-based scaffolds
author: Catherine A. Sword
materials: Aspirate the solution from the scaffolds.

steps.title: Seed fibroblasts onto scaffolds with fibronectin
steps.instruction: Seed fibroblasts onto 3.5 mm broccoli scaffolds at the desired density while including 50 µg/mL human plasma fibronectin (Corning #354008) in the final culture medium.

substeps.instruction: Dilute trypsinized cells to the required concentration (e.g., for 1,000 cells per scaffold dilute to 10,000 cells/mL).
Prepare a 100 µg/mL fibronectin solution in growth medium.
Add 100 µL cell suspension and 100 µL fibronectin solution to each scaffold (gives 1,000 cells and 50 µg/mL fibronectin).
Alternatively, seed cells at any desired density, allow attachment, then replace medium with medium containing 50 µg/mL fibronectin.

steps.title: Culture cells for three days
steps.instruction: Incubate the seeded scaffolds under standard culture conditions for 3 days (shorter times yield less fibronectin ECM).

steps.title: PBS rinse before fixation
steps.instruction: Aspirate the culture medium without touching the scaffold, then add 200 µL sterile PBS to each scaffold. For 6.5 mm scaffolds that fill a 96‑well bottom, tilt the plate and aspirate to the top surface only, avoiding contact with the scaffold.

steps.title: Fix cells with 4 % formaldehyde
steps.instruction: Fix cells by adding 200 µL 4 % formaldehyde in DPBS‑/- and incubating at room temperature for 30 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 4 % formaldehyde in Dulbecco's Phosphate‑Buffered Saline without calcium and magnesium (DPBS‑/-; Gibco #14190-144) by diluting 16 % formaldehyde stock (Electron Microscopy Sciences #100503-914, CAS 50‑00‑0).
Add 200 µL of the freshly prepared 4 % formaldehyde solution to each scaffold.
Incubate at room temperature for 00:30:00.

steps.title: Wash scaffolds three times with PBS
steps.instruction: Remove fixative and rinse the scaffolds three consecutive times with 200 µL PBS each.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate as much liquid as possible without touching the scaffold.
Add 200 µL PBS, aspirate, and repeat two more times.

steps.title: Block and permeabilize scaffolds
steps.instruction: Incubate scaffolds with blocking/permeabilization solution for 1 hour at room temperature (or overnight at 4 °C), followed by an additional 5‑minute room‑temperature incubation.

substeps.instruction: Prepare blocking/permeabilization solution: dissolve 3 % (w/v) BSA (Sigma #A7030-100G), 1 % (w/v) gelatin from cold‑water fish skin (Sigma #G7041-100G, 100 g), and 0.02 % (w/v) saponin (Sigma #G7041-100G) in DPBS‑/- (Gibco #14190-144).
Add 200 µL of this solution to each scaffold.
Incubate for 01:00:00 at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C.
After the incubation, continue at room temperature for an additional 00:05:00.

steps.title: Primary antibody staining
steps.instruction: Stain scaffolds with rabbit anti‑human fibronectin primary antibody, then wash three times with PBS.

substeps.instruction: Prepare primary staining solution: 2 % (v/v) BSA and rabbit‑anti‑human fibronectin polyclonal antibody (Merck MilliporeSigma #F3648) diluted 1:300 in DPBS‑/-.
Aspirate the blocking solution completely.
Add 200 µL primary staining solution to each scaffold.
Incubate for 01:00:00 at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C.
Wash three times with 200 µL PBS (aspirate then add PBS, repeat).

steps.title: Secondary antibody and counterstain
steps.instruction: Apply secondary antibody, DAPI, and phalloidin, then wash three times with PBS.

substeps.instruction: Prepare secondary staining solution in PBS: 2 % (v/v) BSA, donkey anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 546 (Thermo Fisher #A10040) diluted 1:500, DAPI (Sigma #D8417) at 5 µg/mL, and Acti‑Stain 488 Phalloidin (Cytoskeleton Inc. #PHDG1) diluted 1:400.
Aspirate the primary antibody solution completely.
Add 200 µL secondary staining solution to each scaffold.
Incubate for 01:00:00 at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C.
Wash three times with 200 µL PBS (aspirate then add PBS, repeat).

steps.title: Transfer scaffolds to imaging dish
steps.instruction: Using forceps, invert each scaffold onto a cover‑glass‑bottomed dish or chamber (e.g., Ibidi 80807), add enough PBS to keep the scaffold hydrated but not floating, ensuring the scaffold lies flat for imaging.

steps.title: Image scaffolds by confocal microscopy
steps.instruction: Immediately image the stained scaffolds on an inverted confocal microscope (e.g., Leica Stellaris 8) using the following settings: DAPI excited at 405 nm (emission 425‑505 nm), Acti‑Stain 488 Phalloidin excited at 498 nm (emission 505‑547 nm), donkey‑anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 546 excited at 556 nm (emission 561‑814 nm). Acquire DAPI and 488 nm channels sequentially to avoid bleed‑through.
